study type: prospective, randomised controlled, double blinded study
outcome: onset of sensory and motor blockage
peak of sensory and motor blockage
duration of sensory and motor blockage
regression of sensory and motor blockage
hemodynamic parameters (heart rate, systolic blood Pressure, diastolic blood pressure, mean arterial pressure, SpO2)
cohort: 60 patients over 20 years old with ASA I or II scheduled for cesarean section under spinal anaesthesia.
finding: Levobupivacaine provided prolonged sensory blockade and analgesia, earlier regression of motor blockade, more stable hemodynamics, and decreased incidence of adverse effects compared to bupivacaine.
